newsitem.title: GHANA: Malaysians top bidders for Ghana Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: Malaysians top bidders for Ghana Telecom stake.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Berhad has emerged as top bidder for a strategic stake in a privatised Ghana Telecom, offering $38 million for a 30 percent holding and the right to manage the company.
Mohamad Nasir Bin Abdul Razak, head of Network Management of Malaysia Telekom, told Reuters at a ceremony here on Monday that his company's offer was the highest.

A consortium consisting of African Communications Group, Western Wireless and Ghana National Petroleum Co emerged as the top bidder for the right to set up a rival national network of fixed telecommunications services, with an offer of $10.1 million, a spokeswoman for the consortium said.
But officials said President Jerry Rawlings had to ratify all deals before any official announcement could be made.
Razak pledged a major investment programme.

"We will carry out an expansion program of at least 200,000 lines over the next five years, as well as improve the quality of service in many aspects, among others the speed of repairs and the rapidity with which the operator helps you," he said.

In June 1996, Ghana Telecom had about 100,000 telephone lines installed and 6,000 mobile cellular subscribers, according to a memorandum by the Ministry of Tranport and Communications. In the second half of 1996, the government planned to install 100,000 new lines, raising the total to 200,000, or 1.3 telephone per 100 inhabitants.
Present estimated demand was at least 200,000 lines, according to the memorandum.
"We are very happy that we have won," Monique Maddy, president of African Communications Group, told Reuters after the bids were opened for the rival network, which is meant to create competition.

Western Wireless is a cellular provider in the United States. African Communications Group has been operating wireless card pay telephones and a pager system in Tanzania since 1993. The consortium plans to invest between $40 million and $70 million in the coming five years.
Also present at the opening of bids were Deutsche Telekom, but absent were AT&T and Southwestern Bell, initially tipped as top of the list of 13 pre- qualified bidders for both offers.
Both U.S. companies pulled out because they found the procedure too slow, or not transparent enough, according to a source involved in the privatisation.
The invitation for bids was made last February. The state plans to sell a further 21 percent of its holding, most likely by sale to the public, but precisely how and when remains unclear.
In 1994, Ghana Telecom's total revenues amounted to $61 million against $72 million in 1993. Total operating costs were $42 million against $49 million in 1993.

Net income was $7.105 million in 1994 against $10.49 million in 1993. The value of total assets was $214 million in 1994, including $72 million current assets, against $121 million in 1993, including $67 million current assets.
Total liabilities amounted to $272 million in 1994, including $235 million in long term debt. In 1993, total liabilities amounted to $160 million, including $128 million in long-term debt.
